title: Steak Boston
description: Scotch fillet coated in Creole spice and served with a red wine butter sauce. Bold, spiced, and full of character.

ingredients.notes: Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

method.instruction: Mix paprika, chilli powder, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, and thyme into a Creole spice blend.
Coat both sides of the scotch fillets generously with the spice blend, pressing it on firmly.
Heat a heavy-based pan or grill over high heat. Cook fillets for 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Remove and rest on a warm plate.
For the sauce: melt half the butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 2–3 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any spice residue and browned bits from the steak. Let it reduce by half, about 1–2 minutes.
Remove from heat and swirl in the remaining butter until melted and glossy. Season with salt.
Plate the steak and spoon the red wine butter sauce over the top.

notes.title: Creole Spice
notes.content: The Creole spice blend is the signature of this dish — a dry coating that forms a flavourful, slightly blackened crust when seared. No demi glace is used. The sauce is a simple red wine and butter reduction that deglazes the pan and captures the spice residue from the steak.
